The Director
Repatriation General Hospital
216 Daws Road
Daw Park, 5041

11/02/2018

Dear Sir/ Madam,

Re: Mrs Diane Carpenter, aged 58

Thank you for taking over the care of Mrs Carpenter, a breast cancer survivor receiving Tamoxifen after her mastectomy in 1988, who underwent left lung resection following a recent finding of cancer. She will be transferred to your care on 24 May for further management.

Post-operatively, Mrs Carpenter has developed pneumonia, which was treated with antibiotics and ventilation in ICU.Having resolved this complication, she has then received a range of interventions including fluid and nutritional management, oxygen therapy and physiotherapy. However, her mobility has not improved as expected, with her reluctance to mobilise, which complicates her difficulty in coping with her illness.

Mrs Carpenter will require continuous physiotherapy with encouragement to mobilise in addition to monitoring her response to antibiotics and Tamoxifen.  Also, would you please arrange a psychiatric counselling, optimally involving her daughters, from whom her only support is, for adapting coping strategies and emotional support?Please note that her first chemotherapy appointment is arranged on 6 June at Flinders Medical Centre.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Nurse (175W)
